historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Macrolide antibiotics
history.scopeNote: Basis scope: erythromycin-derived lineage; first-screen chronology and macrolide priority unresolved.

starting.description: Within the erythromycin-derived lineage, active microbial erythromycin A supplied a working parent for deliberate derivative programs. The original patent reports active culture product and recovery; Bright 1988 explicitly states spectrum and pharmacokinetic objectives. The precise initial soil-screen sequence remains unestablished.

inspiration.description: Antibacterial activity of the erythromycin-producing soil actinomycete and its natural product; later derivatives were made from the already active antibiotic.

steps.description: A soil isolate produced measurable antibacterial material, which the inventors cultured and isolated as erythromycin.

Erythromycin A was chemically modified into the cohort agents clarithromycin and azithromycin. Researchers sought changes in acid stability, pharmacokinetics and antibacterial spectrum; an erythromycin-derived aza-macrolide series added nitrogen to a 15-membered ring.

design.description: Researchers cultivated and purified the natural antibiotic, then chemically modified erythromycin A to obtain semisynthetic derivatives. In the aza-macrolide series, inserting nitrogen and expanding the ring generated new structures with altered antibacterial spectra as well as pharmacokinetic aims.

circumstances.description: The later search for chemically modified erythromycin derivatives with altered spectrum and improved properties was deliberate; the circumstances of first detection are not established by the patent sections read.

limits: The review describes pikromycin as the first isolated macrolide; the separately produced natural product is not asserted to be a direct precursor of azithromycin or clarithromycin, and its priority has not been independently adjudicated.
The record's cohort lineage is erythromycin A to its semisynthetic derivatives; it does not trace each other natural or later macrolide individually.
conflicts: S2 identifies pikromycin as the first isolated macrolide in 1950; S6 identifies erythromycin as the first discovered macrolide in 1949. Whether the discrepancy reflects discovery versus isolation or other differences was not established; no priority winner is asserted.
gaps: The 1952 Ilotycin original journal paper was located by verified metadata but not read; the exact first-screen chronology remains unestablished.
The 1950 pikromycin preliminary report and the full 1951 pikromycin paper were not read; sources do not establish which compound was discovered first.
The Morimoto et al. 1984 clarithromycin synthesis report was located but not read; the cohort parentage is supported by S2.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Erythromycin came from a soil microorganism isolated by plating and culturing; later macrolides inherit this natural-product lead.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: Natural-product ancestry qualifies under the broad observation definition, but the documented discovery required laboratory work and does not establish a human clinical or population contribution.
